review: skipped: removed 702.11a, 702.11h, which the triage classifies definitional (static-ability marker and redundancy), so they need neither a scenario nor a skip.

702.11b-2: wrong rule outcome. The scenario claimed Doom Blade still resolves after its target gains hexproof; under 608.2b the target is rechecked on resolution and hexproof makes it illegal for A's spell, so Doom Blade fizzles. Rewrote the base to fizzle, made no_response the does_not_fire variant, dropped the Gods Willing variant (protection, 702.16) with its Plains.
702.11d-1: the base carried a non-empty delta; fixed Doom Blade as the spell checked in the decisions and made Shock the one-fact swap.

702.11f-1: Raddic, Tal Zealot is white and black, so Doom Blade (nonblack creature only) could never target it whatever its hexproof; replaced Doom Blade with Last Gasp (black, any creature) and fixed the base's non-empty delta.
702.11g-1: the base carried a non-empty delta; fixed Shock as the source checked in the decisions and made Aether Spellbomb's ability the one-fact swap.
triage/702.11.jsonl: was missing; wrote it (702.11b to 702.11g legality, 702.11b also resolution; 702.11, 702.11a and 702.11h definitional).

scenarios.title: A hexproof permanent cannot be targeted by spells or abilities its controller's opponents control
decisions: A checks whether Shock (paid with Mountain) can target Gladecover Scout.

variants.label: spell_targets_opponents_hexproof
variants.expected: Gladecover Scout is not a legal target for Shock.

variants.label: ability_targets_opponents_hexproof
variants.delta: A checks whether Prodigal Sorcerer's {T} ability can target Gladecover Scout instead of casting Shock.
variants.expected: Gladecover Scout is not a legal target for the ability either.

variants.label: no_hexproof
variants.delta: The target checked is Grizzly Bears, which has no hexproof.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a legal target for Shock.

variants.label: own_hexproof
variants.delta: Gladecover Scout is controlled by A instead of B, and A targets it with Shock.
variants.expected: Gladecover Scout is a legal target for Shock, because hexproof protects it only from its controller's opponents.

scenarios.title: A creature that gains hexproof in response is an illegal target on resolution, so the opposing spell fizzles
decisions: A casts Doom Blade targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping both Swamps.
A passes priority. B casts Snakeskin Veil targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Forest.
Both players pass priority; Snakeskin Veil resolves.
Both players pass priority; Doom Blade tries to resolve.

variants.label: hexproof_in_response
variants.expected: Doom Blade's only target is illegal on resolution and it fizzles. Grizzly Bears stays on the battlefield as a 3/3 with a +1/+1 counter.

variants.label: no_response
variants.delta: B passes without casting Snakeskin Veil.
variants.expected: Doom Blade resolves, and Grizzly Bears is destroyed and moves to B's graveyard.

scenarios.title: A player with hexproof cannot be targeted by their opponents' spells or abilities
decisions: A checks whether Shock (paid with Mountain) can target player B.

variants.label: player_hexproof
variants.expected: Player B is not a legal target for Shock, because B has hexproof from Witchbane Orb.

variants.label: no_orb
variants.delta: Witchbane Orb is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Player B is a legal target for Shock.

variants.label: creature_target
variants.delta: Shock is checked against Grizzly Bears instead of player B.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a legal target for Shock; the player's hexproof does not protect B's permanents.

scenarios.title: Hexproof from a quality stops only opposing spells and abilities with that quality
decisions: A checks whether Doom Blade, paid with Swamp and Mountain, can target Garruk's Harbinger (hexproof from black).

variants.label: black_spell
variants.expected: Garruk's Harbinger is not a legal target for Doom Blade.

variants.label: red_spell
variants.delta: A checks Shock (red), paid with Mountain, instead of Doom Blade.
variants.expected: Garruk's Harbinger is a legal target for Shock.

variants.label: own_harbinger
variants.delta: Garruk's Harbinger is controlled by A instead of B, and A checks Doom Blade.
variants.expected: Garruk's Harbinger is a legal target for Doom Blade, because the ability protects it only from its controller's opponents.

scenarios.title: An effect that makes a permanent lose hexproof removes hexproof from [quality] as well
decisions: A activates Shadowspear's {1} ability, tapping a Swamp; both players pass and it resolves.
A checks whether Doom Blade (paid with the other two Swamps) can target Garruk's Harbinger.

variants.label: hexproof_removed
variants.expected: Garruk's Harbinger has lost its hexproof from black until end of turn and is a legal target for Doom Blade.

variants.label: ability_not_activated
variants.delta: A does not activate Shadowspear's ability.
variants.expected: Garruk's Harbinger is not a legal target for Doom Blade.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's AnimateAll RemoveKeywords$ Hexproof may remove only the plain Hexproof keyword and leave Hexproof:Black.

scenarios.title: An effect that lets a player target creatures as though they lacked hexproof also covers hexproof from [quality]
decisions: A checks whether Doom Blade (paid with both Swamps) can target Garruk's Harbinger.

variants.label: spotlight_controlled
variants.expected: Garruk's Harbinger is a legal target for Doom Blade, because Glaring Spotlight lets A target it as though it lacked hexproof.

variants.label: no_spotlight
variants.delta: Glaring Spotlight is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Garruk's Harbinger is not a legal target for Doom Blade.

variants.label: opponent_spotlight
variants.delta: Glaring Spotlight is controlled by B instead of A.
variants.expected: Garruk's Harbinger is not a legal target for Doom Blade, because the permission applies only to the spotlight controller's spells and abilities.

scenarios.title: Hexproof from two qualities behaves as two separate hexproof abilities
decisions: A checks whether Last Gasp, paid with Swamp and Plains, can target Raddic, Tal Zealot (hexproof from white, hexproof from black).

variants.label: black_spell
variants.expected: Raddic, Tal Zealot is not a legal target for Last Gasp.

variants.label: white_spell
variants.delta: A checks Pacifism (white Aura spell), paid with Plains and Mountain, instead of Last Gasp.
variants.expected: Raddic, Tal Zealot is not a legal target for Pacifism.

variants.label: red_spell
variants.delta: A checks Shock (red), paid with Mountain, instead of Last Gasp.
variants.expected: Raddic, Tal Zealot is a legal target for Shock.

scenarios.title: Hexproof from each color stops every colored source and lets colorless sources through
decisions: A checks whether Shock, paid with Mountain, can target Breaker of Creation (hexproof from each color).

variants.label: red_spell
variants.expected: Breaker of Creation is not a legal target for Shock.

variants.label: colorless_ability
variants.delta: A checks Aether Spellbomb's return-to-hand ability (a colorless source), paid with Island and sacrificing the Spellbomb, instead of Shock.
variants.expected: Breaker of Creation is a legal target for the ability of the colorless Aether Spellbomb.
